name: AdvancedEncryption.WE.Exotic.canonical_linear_test_hsp
title: Canonical labels plus known-scalar multiplication turn a linear-test interface into an abelian hidden-subgroup instance
statement: Let R be a commutative ring, F : R -> S injective (a canonical label of hidden values) and s in R hidden. Then F(x + y s) = F(x' + y' s) iff (x - x') + (y - y') s = 0, i.e. the map (x, y) -> F(x + y s) is constant exactly on the cosets of L_s = {(a, b) : a + b s = 0}; and L_s determines s (if a + b s = 0 <-> a + b t = 0 for all a, b then s = t). Over ZMod p this is an abelian hidden-subgroup problem solved by Shor's algorithm, so any instantiation of the Hair-Sahai / Jutla generic-group interface with canonical labels and efficient multiplication by arbitrary known scalars is quantumly broken.
